meta.title: FORGE — MMA Strength, Power & Conditioning Library
equipment_allowed: Bumper Plates / Lifting Platform (for Olympic-lift variants)

Novice.grip_work: Submaximal — build tissue tolerance, no max holds to failure
Novice.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2, technical round work at 50-60% output
Novice.notes: Own the basic patterns (squat/hinge/press/pull) and build tissue tolerance (neck, grip, low back) before any max-effort or live-pace conditioning. No barbell work above 65% e1RM, no Olympic-lift variants yet.

Beginner.grip_work: Timed holds submaximal (60-70% of max hang time)
Beginner.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2-3, rounds at 60-70% output, technical focus
Beginner.notes: Add posterior-chain, grip and rotational-power volume. Conditioning starts to take on MMA round shape (5min blocks) rather than generic intervals.

Intermediate.grip_work: Max-effort timed holds 1x/week, submaximal the rest
Intermediate.notes: Olympic-lift variants (hang clean/jerk/KB snatch) enter the pool for hip-power transfer to takedowns and striking. Contrast method (heavy lift + explosive movement) becomes the main power tool.

Advanced.grip_work: Max hangs/holds programmed and tracked like a main lift
Advanced.conditioning_intensity: Zone 4-5, fight-pace intervals at 85-95% output, sport-specific work-capacity blocks
Advanced.notes: Full camp periodization (GPP -> SPP -> Peak -> Taper). Heavy strength/power sessions kept 48-72h from live sparring/wrestling/rolling. Conditioning volume matches actual fight length (3x5 amateur or 5x5 title-fight pace).

Elite.intensity_main: 85-97% e1RM, RPE 8-10 only in peak block
Elite.intensity_power: Max intent, autoregulated by bar speed
Elite.grip_work: Fully individualized off actual grip/clinch fatigue data from training
Elite.conditioning_intensity: Fight-simulation pace, opponent-modeled round pacing, HRV/lactate-guided intensity
Elite.notes: S&C fully subordinate to the fight calendar, built backward from fight night. Load is set by daily readiness data, not the written number — the written plan is a default the coach is expected to override.

round_format_reference.Amateur: 3 rounds x 3min work / 1min rest (some commissions use 3x2)

global_rules: Full commercial gym on-site — all barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, cable/machine, and conditioning equipment listed above is available without restriction; no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.

Every session follows this order: explosive/power work (throw_power) first -> main strength lift -> grip/neck/core last -> gas-tank conditioning only on a day NOT preceded by a heavy strength session.

MMA is the highest total training-load sport of the four covered so far (striking + wrestling + ground work all in the same week) — S&C volume should be the LOWEST of any discipline in this library at the same level; the skill work is doing most of the conditioning already.

Olympic-lift variants (hang clean/jerk/KB snatch) are Intermediate-level-and-up only, same rule as the grappling library — Novice/Beginner train the same power quality through trap-bar jumps, KB swings, and med-ball throws.
Reverse Hyper doubles as posterior-chain builder (loaded, strength days) and spinal-decompression recovery tool (bodyweight pendulum, high reps, day after hard sparring/wrestling/rolling).

Heavy squat/hinge/pull sessions are placed 48h+ from live sparring, wrestling, or rolling wherever the weekly schedule allows — this is harder to guarantee in MMA than single-discipline sports, so the coach should treat this as the first thing to protect when the schedule gets tight.

Choose ONE fight-style emphasis per camp based on the actual matchup (opponent's wrestling vs. striking threat) rather than trying to develop all qualities equally in fight week — the Balanced template is the correct DEFAULT outside of fight-specific camps.
Deload every 4th week at 40-50% volume reduction for Intermediate and above.

Fight week: strength work stops 6-7 days out (earlier than single-discipline sports, since weight-cut and skill-taper load are also competing for recovery capacity); only light trap-bar jumps or med-ball throws remain up to 3 days out, then full rest.
